players.product: US utility - UHV transformer buyer (Hyosung HICO end customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 recurring (non-GAAP) EPS of $0.87, in line with expectations, versus $0.96 a year ago; GAAP EPS $0.14 after a non-cash after-tax charge of $111.4 million ($0.30 per share) on the carrying value of Aquarion Water Company at closing and an after-tax charge of $164 million ($0.43 per share) to increase the offshore wind contingent liability. The recurring decline came from lower Electric Transmission earnings (the March FERC base ROE reduction to 9.57%) and lower Gas Distribution, partly offset by higher Electric Distribution revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 recurring EPS $0.87 (vs $0.96 a year ago); GAAP EPS $0.14

quarterly_data.signal: Reaffirmed 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $4.52 to $4.72 per share (revised in March for the 9.57% base transmission ROE and the Aquarion sale) and long-term EPS growth of 5% to 7%, with management pointing to the upper half of that range and growth accelerating around 2028. Management declined to publish a separate rate base growth target, noting historical rate base growth has been slightly over an 8% CAGR and can be derived from the capital slides.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 EPS guidance $4.52 to $4.72 reaffirmed; 5% to 7% long-term growth, upper half; historical rate base CAGR slightly over 8%

quarterly_data.signal: Reaffirmed the five-year capital plan of $21.5 billion of utility infrastructure investment by segment. For the first time the company highlighted the potential increase to that capital forecast from the ISO New England preliminary transmission RFP selection and from AMI in Connecticut - neither is inside the $21.5 billion yet. This is the grid transmission and distribution spend that drives Eversource's transformer, substation and line-equipment procurement.
quarterly_data.figure: $21.5 billion five-year capital plan reaffirmed; transmission RFP and Connecticut AMI upside not yet included

quarterly_data.signal: ISO New England preliminarily selected the joint Eversource/Avangrid proposal from the six bids submitted into its 2025 longer-term transmission planning RFP: a $2.2 billion project to increase transmission capacity between Maine and New Hampshire and strengthen the interface between Northern and Southern New England, with an anticipated in-service date of 2032. Eversource's share is approximately $700 million, of which about half (50%) of the capex would be incurred inside the current five-year forecast period. Milestones: stakeholder comments August 14, ISO New England review and response in August and September, final recommendation anticipated in September, and roll-in to the capital plan at the third quarter call. Second competitive transmission award for Eversource after the Boston 2028 solution study project.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.2 billion project; ~$700 million Eversource share; ~50% inside the five-year plan; in-service 2032
quarterly_data.counterparty: Avangrid (joint bidder); ISO New England (selecting grid operator)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center framing from the CEO: 'if we want to capture economic opportunities around data centers and welcome them to the region, additional generation and expansion of gas capacity is critical.' Eversource has directly supported 2.5 thousand megawatts of new generation coming into the New England region since last year, 80% of which is now online, but says more is needed to support the growing electric demand across New England; energy supply remains the greatest affordability challenge and Eversource neither controls nor profits from it. No interconnection queue, signed or committed data-center megawatts, or large-load customer figures were disclosed on this call.
quarterly_data.figure: 2.5 thousand megawatts of new regional generation supported since last year, 80% online

quarterly_data.signal: Grid equipment procurement: the CL&P filing includes an AMI plan for Connecticut of nearly $1 billion of capital investment plus $300 million of O&M expense. Outside the rate case Eversource requested an expedited decision to move this fall specifically to take advantage of contractual pricing it had locked down with the vendors used for the Massachusetts AMI program (vendors not named); if approved it would mobilize next year and take approximately five years to complete, so part of the $1 billion falls beyond the current forecast period. The benefit-cost analysis is slightly positive nominally but negative on an NPV basis because the docket sat open for years while equipment costs rose - benefits unchanged, cost component increased.
quarterly_data.figure: Connecticut AMI ~$1 billion capital + $300 million O&M; ~five-year rollout; Massachusetts vendor pricing locked; costs risen since original analysis

quarterly_data.signal: CL&P general rate review filed July 14, the first since 2017: revenue deficiency of $451 million at a proposed ROE of 10.25%, an 11% impact on the total customer bill, with approximately 90% of the deficiency from capital investment, storm resiliency investment, storm restoration costs, depreciation and taxes and only 11% from increased O&M. Eversource has invested over $4 billion upgrading Connecticut electric distribution since 2017 across 1.3 million customers in 157 cities and towns, and frames continued investment as needed for aging infrastructure, more frequent severe weather, and the upgrades required to support growing electric demand in the state. Separately, New Hampshire approved an annual base rate adjustment of approximately $24 million effective August 1.
quarterly_data.figure: $451 million revenue deficiency, ~90% capital-driven; over $4 billion invested in Connecticut distribution since 2017

quarterly_data.signal: New England generation coming online: Revolution Wind is over 95%, about 97% complete and is already delivering over 300 megawatts of capacity to the ISO New England grid, ramping toward its full target with a commercial operation date later this year; every component needed to install it is already on hand and the remaining installation is described as straightforward. Two stop-work orders caused the loss of an installation vessel that had to be remobilized, driving the $164 million after-tax charge taken this quarter against the contingent liability Eversource retained on the sale of the project.
quarterly_data.figure: ~97% complete; over 300 megawatts already delivering to the ISO New England grid; $164 million after-tax charge
